question.prompt: The diagonal \(AC\) of square \(ABCD\) has length 8. Find the area of the square.

solutions.explanation: The area of a square equals half the product of its diagonals: \(8\times8\div2=32\).
solutions.title: Use the diagonal-area formula

solutions.explanation:
Let \(s>0\) be the side length of the square. Diagonal \(AC\) is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with two legs of length \(s\), so the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
2s^2=8^2,\qquad s^2=32.
\]
The square's area is \(s^2\), so its area is \(32\).
solutions.title: Find the side length squared
